newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska cattle market quiet, no sales - trade.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska cattle market quiet, no sales - trade.

text.p: Nebraska feedlot cattle markets were quiet near midday Thursday, with no reported sales, according to market sources.
Packer bids were light at $106.00 to $108.00 per cwt on a dressed basis, with asking levels of $108.00 to $109.00.
About 45,800 head sold during the week, USDA said.
A few beef packing plants were short on supply and picking up cattle within a few days of buying them, the sources said.
This week's extreme cold slowed weight gains on cattle that were barely market ready, which was resulting in a few extra cattle being carried over into next week.
